page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n4-standard-8 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, return mid-range scores, with Geekbench recording a single-core score of 1770.0 and a multi-core score of 6838.0. Memory read bandwidth is measured at 530.44 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 61.33 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, while the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25% tier. For specialized tasks, the hardware-assisted instruction sets enable steady performance in cryptography and image processing, but multi-threaded decompression and text-generation tasks on larger models, such as 7B parameter LLMs, show weaker performance, with text generation dropping to 6.31 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for mainstream business applications without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Its dedicated CPU allocation and standard memory-to-core ratio make it a reliable option for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 12.95 GB/sec, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference using small models. However, workloads requiring high-speed local storage, massive memory capacity, or intensive multi-threaded decompression may encounter performance bottlenecks due to the lack of local NVMe drives and the lower memory performance tier.
